verification: The derivative of a finite sum is the sum of the derivatives.
For k<n, derivative is (n-k)*a_k*x^(n-k-1); for k=n the term is constant and its derivative is zero.
Therefore P'(x)=sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(n-k)*a_k*x^(n-k-1), exactly the visible expanded formula.
For a constant polynomial the independent derivative is zero; this edge case is not a reconstruction of prior text.

verification: For an arbitrary point x0 under the printed hypotheses, differentiability of v implies continuity at x0, hence v stays nonzero sufficiently near x0.
With u0=u(x0), v0=v(x0), du=u(x0+h)-u0 and dv=v(x0+h)-v0, the quotient difference divided by h equals (v0*(du/h)-u0*(dv/h))/(v0*(v0+dv)).
The numerator order, subtraction sign, prime placement and squared denominator in the visible theorem agree.
